State legislatures appoint delegates to the convention of states.

assumptions.text: The current system of congressional proposal and ratification is sufficient to protect fundamental rights.

Recall mechanisms for delegates are credible and enforceable in practice.
There is continuity between current legislative behavior and expected behavior under a convention.
Fear of losing Second Amendment rights is more likely driven by political rhetoric than actual legislative threat.
